title: Latency bakeoff run notes — 2025-07-08
content:
Purpose:
Run and capture the results of the latency bakeoff comparing kernel-v2.3.1 (current stable) vs kernel-v2.4-experimental with optimizations for KV cache handling and attention kernel micro-tiling. The goal was to test tail latency (p95/p99), cold-start prefix impact, and behavior under bursty QPS with real-ish traces.

Date / time:
2025-07-08 09:30–11:10 PT

Attendees:
- Marina Kovalenko (owner)
- Diego Martinez (bench infra)
- Priya Shah (runtime engineer)
- Ethan Wong (observability)
- Samira Ali (SRE)

Quick summary:
- kernel-v2.4-experimental shows 6–9% improvement in p50 and ~12% improvement in p95 for the small-embed chat workload on A100s when using the new KV eviction heuristics and fused attention kernel.
- p99 still regressed in a few burst scenarios (spikes to 3.5x baseline) — seems correlated with concurrent cache-miss storms at high concurrency (>=48).
- Quantized FP16->INT8 path (q8fz) produced ~18% throughput improvement but introduced a 2–4% rate of short decoding errors in a specific model variant (gpt-small-2024-q8f). We flagged and paused those runs.

Environments used:
- Cluster: bench-rig-14 (A100 40GB), bench-rig-21 (H100 80GB) used for cross-checks
- Runtime build: kernel-v2.3.1 (sha: a1b2c3d) and kernel-v2.4-experimental (sha: f9e8d7c)
- Model: chat-lite-4b / chat-lite-4b-q8f for quantized runs
- Sequence lengths: seq=256 (typical), seq=1024 (tail test)
- Batch sizes: 1, 4, 8, 16
- Concurrency profiles: steady 120 qps (low), ramp 0->400 qps (burst), spike tests with 600 concurrent requests for 30s
- Request pattern: replayed production prefix traces from 2025-06-30 (trace-id batch supplied by Diego)

Commands / flags (representative):
- benchctl run --config bakeoff-v2.json --kernel kernel-v2.3.1 --model chat-lite-4b --seq 256 --concurrency 120
- benchctl run --config bakeoff-v2.json --kernel kernel-v2.4-experimental --kv-policy sticky-evict-0.2 --fused-attn on
- benchctl compare --baseline kernel-v2.3.1 --candidate kernel-v2.4-experimental --metrics p50,p95,p99,errors,qps

Key numeric results (median of 5 runs, seq=256, batch=1, concurrency=120):
- kernel-v2.3.1 (baseline): p50=23ms, p95=72ms, p99=155ms, throughput=118 qps
- kernel-v2.4-experimental: p50=21.6ms (-6%), p95=63.4ms (-12%), p99=148ms (-4.5%), throughput=128 qps (+8.5%)
- Notes: error rate stayed <0.01% for both in FP16 path.

Burst / tail tests (ramp to 400 qps, seq=256):
- kernel-v2.3.1: p99 spikes to 520ms during ramp; KV cache warm-up takes ~18s to stabilize.
- kernel-v2.4-experimental: p99 spikes to 450ms during ramp but shows intermittent 1.2–3.5x p99 spikes correlated with periods where >60% of requests miss the prefix cache simultaneously.
- Hypothesis: eviction heuristics in v2.4 occasionally evict popular prefixes during concurrent small-window bursts.

Sequence=1024 runs (headroom / long-context):
- Both kernels see expected linear increase in p50/p95; v2.4's fused-attn reduces p50 by ~9% but p99 remains similar to baseline.

Quantization check (q8f path) — preliminary, limited to H100 rig:
- Throughput: +18% vs FP16 on candidate with batch=4.
- Observed: non-deterministic decoding artifacts for chat-lite-4b-q8f in ~2.7% of samples (truncated token or repeated token chunks).
- Action: disable q8f auto-rollout until we reproduce locally and add unit tests for decoding invariants.

Observability notes (Ethan):
- Tracing shows majority of candidate improvement is in attention kernel time (-22% ms).
- Hotspot: lock acquisition in KV cache on eviction path increased wall-clock for certain threads — need lock-free or sharded eviction mitigation.
- Dashboard: added a temporary panel for "concurrent cache-miss ratio" (Grafana link above).

Unresolved questions / open hypotheses:
1) Why do we get rare 3.5x p99 spikes only on candidate during bursts? Is it a contention artifact or a race in eviction policy?
2) Can we replicate the q8f decoding artifact deterministically with smaller tests? Is this a model-compat or runtime quantization bug?
3) Is H100 showing different eviction contention patterns compared to A100 (observed less severe spikes on H100 but we need more runs)?

Action items (owners and short timeline):
- Priya: add sharded eviction queue prototype and run limited bakeoff (target: PR by 2025-07-15). (PRIYA-1)
- Diego: create deterministic replay that triggers the p99 spike within 10s on bench rigs; attach trace IDs to JIRA RINF-1987 (ETA 2025-07-10). (DIEGO-2)
- Ethan: add CPU-side lock contention metrics to bench agent and correlate with p99 spikes; extend dashboard panels (ETA 2025-07-11). (ETHAN-3)
- Marina: pause q8f rollout and open a separate ticket for decoding artifact; write reproduction checklist and unit test skeleton (ETA 2025-07-09). (MARINA-4)
- Samira: schedule higher-fidelity H100 runs during off-hours to reduce interference; ensure isolation (ETA 2025-07-12). (SAMIRA-5)

Notes to self / informal observations:
- "Notes to self" style: candidate feels promising for steady-state latency-sensitive workloads; the bursty behavior is the gating issue for rollout.
- Keep the eviction policy tunable via config flags so Dedicated customers can pick more conservative defaults.
- Consider adding an adaptive cooldown window after eviction events to avoid synchronized misses.

Follow-up meeting:
- 2025-07-10 10:00 PT — quick sync to review Diego's deterministic replay and initial traces.

Attachments / artifacts to add to this doc: bench logs (bench-2025-07-08-*.tar.gz), trace export (zip), kernel diffs (link to PR above).

End of notes.
